chunks.arabic_text: ٩ - مُصَافٍ، مَوْلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ).

translations.en: 9 – Muṣāfī, the client of Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him).

en.summary: This entry from Al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Ḍuʿafāʾ* identifies Muṣāfī as a mawlā (client) of Imam al-Bāqir (peace be upon him), highlighting the importance of social status and lineage in the evaluation of narrators within Shia hadith sciences. His classification as 'weak' (ḍaʿīf) serves as a critical case study for scholars assessing the reliability of transmitters who, despite their proximity to the Imam, may possess defects in memory or precision. This reflects the rigorous methodology of early Shia scholars in distinguishing between mere association with the Ahl al-Bayt and actual scholarly competence.
en.seo_question: Who is Muṣāfī and what is his status as a narrator in Shia hadith literature?

key_terms.مَوْلَى: Client or freed slave, often indicating a close associate or follower
key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbdillāh, a title for Imam al-Bāqir (peace be upon him)
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ: Weak, a technical term in hadith sciences denoting a narrator with lower reliability
key_terms.رَوَى عَنْهُ: He narrated from him, indicating a transmission relationship
